query:
The group decided to order pizza. What did Soo-Yeon's response to that decision reveal about her actual position, and what specifically in how she responded signals this — given that she did not object?

Options:
A. Soo-Yeon
B. Nadia
C. Lena
D. Kezia
context:
[1] (about=Soo-Yeon, episodic, t4 @2026-03-09T19:26:00) Priya mentioned pizza for tonight. Can we do something lighter? I had a heavy lunch 😅
[2] (about=Soo-Yeon, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:20:00) I'll just have Raj's flatbread.
[3] (about=Priya, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:21:00) lol ok pizza it is i guess 😅 majority wins. Nadia you want in on the order?
[4] (about=Kezia, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:19:00) fine with pizza 🍕
[5] (about=Soo-Yeon, episodic, t4 @2026-03-09T19:13:00) she has good taste in groups 🙂
[6] (about=Lena, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:13:00) so basically Soo-Yeon ran a successful theory of mind intervention tbh. she identified the barrier and reframed the proposition. elegant
[7] (about=Lena, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:10:00) so basically that explains why Nadia didn't push back on Tomasz's Dune ruling even though everyone else was complaining tbh
[8] (about=Marcus, episodic, t10 @2026-03-30T19:46:00) Lena's merchant tile placement in round two signaled she was building toward Coventry. Blocking Dudley removes that route. It's spatial denial, not aggression.
[9] (about=Soo-Yeon, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:20:00) Confirmed 🙂
[10] (about=Soo-Yeon, episodic, t2 @2026-04-06T19:05:00) that was the reasoning, yes 🙂
[11] (about=Soo-Yeon, core, t4 @2026-03-09T19:01:00) Requests lighter food than pizza for tonight due to a heavy lunch.
[12] (about=Soo-Yeon, core, t4 @2026-03-09T19:01:00) Compliments Kezia's taste in groups.
[13] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t6 @2026-03-16T19:01:00) Group decides to order pizza for the session, with majority vote; Nadia opts out.
[14] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t4 @2026-03-09T19:01:00) Tonight's snack changed from pizza to lighter options: rice crackers, hummus, and mixed nuts.
agent_answer:
A. Soo-Yeon.

Her response revealed that she was **not actually in favor of pizza**; she still preferred something lighter because she’d had a heavy lunch. She didn’t object to the group’s majority decision, but her non-objection was **accommodation, not agreement**.

The specific signals: she first asked, **“Can we do something lighter? I had a heavy lunch 😅”**, and then, rather than agreeing to pizza, she said, **“I'll just have Raj's flatbread.”** That alternative order shows she accepted the group’s pizza decision without endorsing it personally.

query:
The group discussed the expectation that everyone should bring either a game or food to the annual marathon. What did Nadia's response signal about her actual relationship to this group norm, and how would you know from what she said?

Options:
A. Nadia
B. Tomasz
C. Marcus
D. Lena
context:
[1] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:06:00) I will bring a game. I do not participate in the food arrangement.
[2] (about=Lena, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:05:00) so basically the norm here is bring something, game or food, agreed tbh. one could argue that even the people who brought nothing last year understood this expectation, they just didn't follow through
[3] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:04:00) In my experience the marathon only works when everyone contributes. It is the social contract of a shared day.
[4] (about=Priya, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:07:00) that totally counts Nadia! honestly a good game pitch is worth more than another bag of chips 😊
[5] (about=Lena, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:10:00) so basically that explains why Nadia didn't push back on Tomasz's Dune ruling even though everyone else was complaining tbh
[6] (about=Nadia, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:36:00) Thank you. I did not say anything but I noticed that as well.
[7] (about=Nadia, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:38:00) I did not want to interrupt the game.
[8] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:07:00) Last April. Nadia found that I was one of the few people in the group who owned the base game for that particular series. We played four sessions over six weeks.
[9] (about=Nadia, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:05:00) Yes. Everyone keep their food away from the card area please.
[10] (about=Priya, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:21:00) lol ok pizza it is i guess 😅 majority wins. Nadia you want in on the order?
[11] (about=Nadia, core, t12 @2026-04-13T19:01:00) Explains she did not want to interrupt the game, hence not mentioning the food issue.
[12] (about=Nadia, core, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) Will bring a game to the marathon but does not participate in food arrangement.
agent_answer:
**A. Nadia**

Nadia's response signals **partial, selective compliance** with the norm rather than rejection of it.

- The norm (as Lena framed it) is: *bring something — a game or food.* Nadia accepted exactly one half of that: **"I will bring a game. I do not participate in the food arrangement."**
- So she is **not** a norm-breaker: she meets the "bring something" expectation through the game route, and Priya confirms this counts — *"that totally counts Nadia! honestly a good game pitch is worth more than another bag of chips"* [4].
- But she explicitly **opts out of the food-arrangement side** of the norm, declining to take part in that part of the shared contribution.
- How we know: it's right in her own words — the two-part statement pairs an affirmative commitment (bring a game) with a flat refusal (no food arrangement). She never disputes that the norm exists; she just defines her own terms within it.

Note: the other listed people (Tomasz, Marcus, Lena) are not who is being asked about here — Tomasz is the one who articulated the "social contract" framing, and Lena stated the norm itself; Nadia is the one whose response shows partial adherence.
